newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steady, softer undertone developing.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steady, softer undertone developing.

text.p: NWE spot gasoline prices were about steady on Friday but traders said the market was beginning to show a softer undertone with recently supportive trade house hedging absent.
"The swaps related hedging has supported the barge market this week, but there's been very little fundamental demand," a barge broker said.

Summer grade barges were valued around $208 a tonne with winter grade barges heard offered down to $207, buyers were scarce. Barge swaps reflected the weakening sentiment dipping 50 cents to $1 per tonne.
But traders expected these losses to quickly be reversed once the key spring driving season demand kicks-in.

Cargo activity remained thin. Traders said that despite a theoretical arbitrage window to the U.S. there was little sign of product moving transatlantic, although demand in the tighter Mediterranean market was drawing some interest. They said freight costs were restrictive for both options.
Eurograde cargoes valued around $210 a tonne cif NWE with Med values around $219-$220 cif Med.
Saudi Aramco decided not to award its tender for up to 1.5 million barrels of gasoline for April delivery due to the high price of offers, traders said.
Some of the product had been expected to move from Europe because of tight Far East supplies. However, one trader said Aramco may now defer its requirements to May.
